newsitem.title: UK: Doubts cast on proposed cross-England ship canal.
newsitem.headline: Doubts cast on proposed cross-England ship canal.

text.p: A controversial plan to build a ship canal across northern England may never be realised, one of the partners in the consortium behind the project said on Thursday.

The environmental group Friends of the Earth has described the scheme, which would enable ships of 10,000 tonnes ships to sail between the Irish and North seas, as "the most environmentally damaging development proposal in living memory."

Alan Lamerton, managing director of AMEC Civil Engineering, said the Solway Firth-Tyneside canal was technically possible but there were "many factors which could alter, amend or stop the concept in its tracks."
AMEC earlier took part in a presentation to politicians of the plan for the six billion pound ($9.6 billion) project.
Lamerton said in a statement that much work, including environmental impact studies, had to be carried out before any firm proposals could be made for such a huge project.
"In addition to a feasibility study, AMEC believes that any project of this size and complexity must also have the support of politicians and the public", he said.
